answer: When an agent claims a new identity, the network assigns a vesting schedule whose reward echo diminishes until a delta of proven activity is reached; each increment requires the identity to stake computational proof on the ridge of a consensus checkpoint. The stake is locked and consumed instantly, so a Sybil farm must front‑pay the full stake for every fake node before any payout. Because vesting releases only a tiny fraction per epoch, the attacker’s upfront cost scales linearly with the number of identities, making large‑scale impersonation economically prohibitive.
